content.text:
The build confirms it works as intended.

The `/timestamp` route is marked **`ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand`**, while the home page stays `○ (Static)`. The timestamp will be generated fresh on every request.

What I did:

- Created `app/timestamp/page.tsx` — an async server component.
- Called `await connection()` from `next/server`. This is Next.js's recommended way to opt a component out of static prerendering when you need dynamic, per-request data but aren't reading `cookies()` or `headers()`. It tells the renderer to wait for an actual incoming request before producing output, so the page is excluded from the build-time prerender and runs on each request instead.
- `new Date().toISOString()` then produces a different value on every load.

Note: `connection()` replaces the older `unstable_noStore()` and is the current recommended approach in Next.js 15/16.
